title: Transfer: circuits and induction
target: Apply circuit relationships and explain an induction observation.
criteria: Use current and voltage rules in a new circuit.
Account for electrical power and energy.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A 20 V ideal source feeds 10 Ω and 20 Ω resistors in parallel. What are branch currents and total current?
cpa.guide: Each branch has 20 V. Currents are V/R, then add at the junction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 9 V supply powers series resistors 3 Ω and 6 Ω. Which set is consistent?
options: Current 1 A; drops 3 V and 6 V.
Currents 3 A and 1.5 A in the same series loop.
cpa.guide: R_total = 9 Ω; I = 1 A. Drops sum to the source voltage.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A 5 V device draws 0.80 A for 45 s. What input power and energy does it receive?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A motor receives 90 J and provides 54 J of useful motion. Which statement is correct?
options: Efficiency is 60%; 36 J goes to other outputs.
Efficiency is 40%; all 90 J is useful.
cpa.guide: 54/90 = 0.60; conservation accounts for the 36 J difference.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A stationary loop lies in a steady field. It is then rotated so the flux changes. Which sequence is predicted?
options: Constant emf initially; none during rotation.
No sustained induced emf initially; emf can occur during rotation.
No emf is possible because the loop does not move sideways.
cpa.guide: Changing orientation changes flux; steady initial flux produces no Faraday emf.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A coil produces a pulse when a magnet approaches. Which change should reverse pulse sign while leaving the magnet’s pole facing the coil unchanged?
options: Paint the coil a different color.
Increase coil wire length without motion.
Withdraw the magnet along the same path.
cpa.guide: Withdrawal reverses the sign of flux change. Holding still instead makes the motion-induced emf zero.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.
